name: Chapter 8: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
description: Naming, carbonyl structure, preparation, nucleophilic addition, Tollens and Fehling, haloform, aldol, Cannizzaro, acidity, HVZ and uses

cards.term: Aldehyde vs ketone vs carboxylic acid?
cards.definition: C=O bonded to C and H (aldehyde) to two C (ketone) to C/H and –OH (acid). With –NH₂: amide; with halogen: acyl halide.

cards.term: Which are derivatives of carboxylic acids?
cards.definition: Esters and anhydrides (also amides, acyl halides)

cards.term: Natural fragrant aldehydes and their sources?
cards.definition: Vanillin (vanilla beans), salicylaldehyde (meadow sweet), cinnamaldehyde (cinnamon)

cards.term: How are common names of aldehydes formed?
cards.definition: From the common acid name, –ic acid → aldehyde; substituent positions by Greek letters α, β, γ (α = carbon next to CHO)
Name the two groups + ketone acetone for dimethyl ketone alkyl phenyl ketones as acyl + "phenone" (acetophenone, benzophenone)

cards.term: IUPAC suffixes for aldehydes and ketones?
cards.definition: Replace –e with –al / –one aldehyde carbon is C-1 ketone numbered from the end nearer C=O

cards.term: Naming an aldehyde on a ring?
cards.definition: Suffix carbaldehyde after the cycloalkane (ring C bearing CHO = C-1); benzenecarbaldehyde = benzaldehyde (accepted)
Ethanal, 4-bromo-3-methylheptanal, 3-methylcyclopentanone, cyclohexanecarbaldehyde, pent-2-enal, 1-phenylpropan-1-one
3-Oxopentanal, 2,4-dimethylpentan-3-one, 4-nitrobenzaldehyde, propane-1,2,3-tricarbaldehyde
Table 8.1

cards.term: Hybridisation and geometry of carbonyl carbon?
cards.definition: sp², trigonal planar, bond angles ~120°; π bond from p–p overlap with O

cards.term: Why is the carbonyl group polar?
cards.definition: O is more electronegative: resonance between neutral (A) and dipolar (B) C⁺–O⁻

cards.term: Carbonyl carbon and oxygen as acid/base centres?
cards.definition: Carbon: electrophilic (Lewis acid). Oxygen: nucleophilic (Lewis base).
Carbonyl compounds have larger dipole moments: more polar than ethers
Oxidation of 1° → aldehyde, 2° → ketone; or dehydrogenation over Ag / Cu (volatile alcohols, industrial)
Ozonolysis then Zn dust + H₂O → aldehydes/ketones by substitution pattern
Ethyne → acetaldehyde; all other alkynes → ketones
Acyl chloride + H₂ over Pd–BaSO₄ → aldehyde (benzoyl chloride → benzaldehyde)

cards.term: Why is Pd poisoned with BaSO₄ in Rosenmund? (insight)
cards.definition: To stop reduction at the aldehyde (unpoisoned Pd would go on to the alcohol)
Nitrile + SnCl₂ + HCl → imine (RCH=NH); hydrolysis → aldehyde
Selective reduction to imine, then H₂O → aldehyde; C=C untouched
Esters → aldehydes
Toluene + CrO₂Cl₂ (chromyl chloride) in CS₂ → chromium complex; H₃O⁺ → benzaldehyde
→ benzylidene diacetate; aqueous acid → benzaldehyde

cards.term: Why do these reagents stop at the aldehyde?
cards.definition: They convert CH₃ into an intermediate (complex / diacetate) that is hard to oxidise further
Side-chain chlorination (Cl₂/hν) → benzal chloride; hydrolysis at 373 K
Benzene + CO + HCl with anhyd. AlCl₃ / CuCl → benzaldehyde
With dialkylcadmium R₂Cd (from Grignard + CdCl₂)
Grignard reagent then hydrolysis: CH₃CH₂CN + C₆H₅MgBr → propiophenone
Benzene + RCOCl / ArCOCl with anhyd. AlCl₃ → aryl ketone

cards.term: Aldehyde and ketone name reactions: reagents
cards.definition: Rosenmund: H₂ / Pd–BaSO₄ on RCOCl; Stephen: SnCl₂ + HCl on RCN, then H₃O⁺; Etard: CrO₂Cl₂ on toluene; Gattermann–Koch: CO + HCl, AlCl₃/CuCl on benzene; Friedel–Crafts acylation: RCOCl + anhyd. AlCl₃

cards.term: Physical state of methanal and ethanal?
cards.definition: Methanal: gas. Ethanal: volatile liquid. Others: liquid or solid.

cards.term: Why do aldehydes/ketones boil higher than hydrocarbons and ethers but lower than alcohols?
cards.definition: Dipole–dipole association; but no intermolecular H-bonding
n-butane 273 < methoxyethane 281 < propanal 322 < acetone 329 < propan-1-ol 370 K

cards.term: Why are lower aldehydes/ketones miscible with water?
cards.definition: Carbonyl O accepts H-bonds from water; solubility falls with chain length
Lower aldehydes: sharp, pungent; larger ones more fragrant (perfumes, flavours)

cards.term: Increasing b.p. (Example 8.2): butanal, butan-1-ol, ethoxyethane, n-pentane?
cards.definition: n-Pentane < ethoxyethane < butanal < butan-1-ol

cards.term: Increasing b.p. (Intext 8.3): CH₃CHO, CH₃CH₂OH, CH₃OCH₃, CH₃CH₂CH₃?
cards.definition: CH₃CH₂CH₃ < CH₃OCH₃ < CH₃CHO < CH₃CH₂OH

cards.term: Alkenes vs carbonyls: type of addition?
cards.definition: Alkenes: electrophilic addition. Carbonyls: nucleophilic addition.
Nu attacks C ~perpendicular to the sp² plane → tetrahedral alkoxide (sp² → sp³); it takes up H⁺

cards.term: Why are aldehydes more reactive than ketones? (2 reasons)
cards.definition: Steric: one bulky group vs two. Electronic: two alkyl groups (+I) reduce electrophilicity more.

cards.term: Is benzaldehyde more or less reactive than propanal? (Example 8.3)
cards.definition: Less: resonance with the ring reduces the polarity of C=O

cards.term: Increasing reactivity (Intext 8.4): ethanal, propanal, propanone, butanone?
cards.definition: Butanone < propanone < propanal < ethanal

cards.term: Increasing reactivity: benzaldehyde, p-tolualdehyde, p-nitrobenzaldehyde, acetophenone?
cards.definition: Acetophenone < p-tolualdehyde < benzaldehyde < p-nitrobenzaldehyde
Pure HCN is slow; base makes CN⁻, a stronger nucleophile → cyanohydrin (useful synthetic intermediate)
Crystalline bisulphite addition compound, water-soluble; regenerated by dilute acid/alkali: used to separate and purify aldehydes

cards.term: Why does the bisulphite equilibrium favour aldehydes, not ketones?
cards.definition: Steric reasons: lies right for most aldehydes, left for most ketones
1 ROH → hemiacetal; 2nd ROH → acetal (gem-dialkoxy)
Cyclic ethylene glycol ketal; acetals/ketals hydrolyse back with aqueous acid

cards.term: Role of dry HCl in acetal formation?
cards.definition: Protonates carbonyl O, making C more electrophilic

cards.term: Carbonyl + H₂N–Z: product and why it forms?
cards.definition: >C=N–Z via a carbinolamine acid-catalysed rapid dehydration drives it
Table 8.2
Yellow, orange or red solids for characterising aldehydes and ketones
NaBH₄ / LiAlH₄ / H₂-catalyst: aldehyde → 1°, ketone → 2° alcohol
>C=O → >CH₂ with Zn–Hg + conc. HCl
>C=O + NH₂NH₂ → hydrazone; KOH / ethylene glycol, heat → >CH₂ + N₂

cards.term: Clemmensen vs Wolff–Kishner: when to choose which? (insight)
cards.definition: Clemmensen is acidic (avoid for acid-sensitive groups); Wolff–Kishner is basic (avoid for base-sensitive groups)
Aldehydes: easily → acids (even mild agents). Ketones: only vigorous conditions, with C–C cleavage → mixture of smaller acids.
Warm aldehyde + ammoniacal AgNO₃ → silver mirror; aldehyde → carboxylate (alkaline)
Fehling A (CuSO₄) + B (alkaline Rochelle salt); aldehyde → red-brown Cu₂O ppt
Aromatic aldehydes (e.g. benzaldehyde); they still give Tollens’
Methyl ketones (CH₃CO–) + NaOX → sodium salt of acid with one C fewer + CHX₃; C=C not affected

cards.term: What does the iodoform test detect?
cards.definition: CH₃CO– or CH₃CH(OH)– groups (yellow CHI₃)

cards.term: Which alcohol and aldehyde give a positive iodoform test? (insight)
cards.definition: Ethanol and ethanal (the only aldehyde); methanol does not

cards.term: Example 8.4: C₈H₈O, 2,4-DNP +, iodoform +, Tollens −, gives C₇H₆O₂ on oxidation. A and B?
cards.definition: A = acetophenone; B = benzoic acid

cards.term: Example 8.4 reactions: A with chromic acid and with NaOI?
cards.definition: Benzoic acid; sodium benzoate + CHI₃
Strong –I of C=O and resonance-stabilised enolate conjugate base
Aldehydes/ketones with ≥1 α-H + dilute alkali → β-hydroxy aldehyde (aldol) or ketone (ketol)
2CH₃CHO → 3-hydroxybutanal (aldol) → −H₂O → but-2-enal
Ba(OH)₂: → 4-hydroxy-4-methylpentan-2-one (ketol) → 4-methylpent-3-en-2-one
Aldehyde + alcohol

cards.term: Cross aldol between ethanal and propanal?
cards.definition: Both have α-H → four products: but-2-enal, 2-methylpent-2-enal (self); 2-methylbut-2-enal, pent-2-enal (cross)

cards.term: Cross aldol with a ketone (Claisen–Schmidt type)?
cards.definition: Benzaldehyde + acetophenone, OH⁻ 293 K → benzalacetophenone (1,3-diphenylprop-2-en-1-one) major

cards.term: Intuition: why does aldol need an α-H?
cards.definition: Base must pull off an α-H to make the enolate nucleophile, which then attacks another carbonyl
Aldehydes with no α-H + conc. alkali, heat: one molecule → alcohol, one → carboxylate (disproportionation)
2HCHO + conc. KOH → CH₃OH + HCOOK
2C₆H₅CHO + conc. NaOH → benzyl alcohol + sodium benzoate

cards.term: Aldol or Cannizzaro? The quick test.
cards.definition: Has α-H + dilute alkali → aldol. No α-H + concentrated alkali → Cannizzaro.
HNO₃/H₂SO₄ at 273–283 K → m-nitrobenzaldehyde (C=O deactivating, meta-directing)
40% HCHO: preserves biological specimens; bakelite, urea–formaldehyde glues
Acetaldehyde: acetic acid, ethyl acetate, vinyl acetate, polymers, drugs. Benzaldehyde: perfumery, dyes. Acetone, ethyl methyl ketone: solvents.
Aliphatic acids C₁₂–C₁₈, occurring as glycerol esters in fats
Replace –e with –oic acid COOH carbon is C-1 multiple COOH: dicarboxylic/tricarboxylic acid
Table 8.3

Benzoic = benzenecarboxylic acid
phenylacetic = 2-phenylethanoic acid
phthalic = benzene-1,2-dicarboxylic acid

cards.term: Why is the carboxyl carbon less electrophilic than a carbonyl carbon?
cards.definition: Resonance with the –OH lone pair

cards.term: Consequence: do acids give typical carbonyl reactions (e.g. with NH₂OH)? (insight)
cards.definition: No: the resonance-reduced C=O doesn’t give aldehyde/ketone addition reactions
KMnO₄ (neutral/acid/alkaline), K₂Cr₂O₇, or CrO₃–H₂SO₄ (Jones reagent)
Vigorous oxidation (chromic acid / KMnO₄): entire side chain → –COOH whatever its length

cards.term: Which alkyl side chain is not oxidised?
cards.definition: Tertiary (no benzylic H)
Hydrolysis (H⁺ or OH⁻): RCN → amide → RCOOH; mild conditions stop at the amide
RMgX + CO₂ (dry ice) → salt; H₃O⁺ → RCOOH

cards.term: Which methods ascend the series (one C more than R–X)?
cards.definition: Nitrile hydrolysis and Grignard + CO₂

cards.term: Acids from acyl halides and anhydrides?
cards.definition: Hydrolysis (water; faster with base then acid)
Acid hydrolysis gives acid directly; basic hydrolysis gives carboxylate, then acidify

Jones
HBr/KCN/H₃O⁺
Mg/CO₂
KMnO₄–KOH
KMnO₄–H₂SO₄
Tollens

cards.term: Convert to benzoic acid (Intext 8.7): ethylbenzene, acetophenone, bromobenzene, styrene?
cards.definition:
KMnO₄–KOH then H₃O⁺
KMnO₄ (or NaOI)
Mg/ether then CO₂, H₃O⁺
KMnO₄ then H₃O⁺

cards.term: State and odour of aliphatic acids?
cards.definition: Up to C₉: colourless liquids, unpleasant odour; higher: wax-like, odourless

cards.term: Why do acids boil higher than alcohols of similar mass?
cards.definition: More extensive H-bonding; exist as dimers even in vapour and aprotic solvents
Up to 4 C miscible decreases with chain length benzoic acid nearly insoluble in cold water

cards.term: Reactions of acids with metals and bases?
cards.definition: Na → salt + H₂ NaOH → salt also NaHCO₃ → CO₂ effervescence (test for –COOH; phenols don’t)
Ionise to resonance-stabilised carboxylate + H₃O⁺

cards.term: pKa of HCl, CF₃COOH, benzoic acid, acetic acid?
cards.definition: −7.0, 0.23, 4.19, 4.76; smaller pKa = stronger acid

cards.text: pKa scale: strong acids {{c1::< 1}}; moderately strong {{c2::1–5}}; weak {{c3::5–15}}; extremely weak {{c4::> 15}}.

cards.term: Why are carboxylic acids stronger than phenols?
cards.definition: Carboxylate: charge on two equivalent O (equivalent resonance). Phenoxide: non-equivalent structures with charge on less electronegative C.

cards.term: Effect of EWG and EDG on acidity?
cards.definition: EWG stabilises carboxylate, increases acidity; EDG destabilises, decreases it
Ph < I < Br < Cl < F < CN < NO₂ < CF₃

cards.term: Acidity order of halo and substituted acetic acids (NCERT)?
cards.definition: CF₃COOH > CCl₃COOH > CHCl₂COOH > NO₂CH₂COOH > NCCH₂COOH > FCH₂COOH > ClCH₂COOH > BrCH₂COOH > HCOOH > ClCH₂CH₂COOH > C₆H₅COOH > C₆H₅CH₂COOH > CH₃COOH > CH₃CH₂COOH

cards.term: Why does phenyl or vinyl directly on COOH increase acidity?
cards.definition: The attached carbon is sp² (more electronegative), outweighing the resonance donation
4.46, 4.19, 3.41

cards.term: Stronger acid (Intext 8.8): CH₃COOH or CH₂FCOOH; CH₂FCOOH or CH₂ClCOOH?
cards.definition: CH₂FCOOH; CH₂FCOOH (F more electronegative)

cards.term: Stronger: CH₂FCH₂CH₂COOH or CH₃CHFCH₂COOH? F₃C–C₆H₄–COOH or CH₃–C₆H₄–COOH?
cards.definition: CH₃CHFCH₂COOH (F closer); 4-CF₃-benzoic acid

cards.term: Intuition: why does distance weaken the –I effect?
cards.definition: Inductive pull passes through σ bonds and fades quickly, roughly halving per bond
Heat with H₂SO₄ or P₂O₅: 2CH₃COOH → ethanoic anhydride
Alcohol/phenol + acid with conc. H₂SO₄ or dry HCl
Nucleophilic acyl substitution: protonation of C=O, alcohol adds (tetrahedral), proton transfer makes –OH₂⁺, water leaves, loss of H⁺
→ acyl chlorides; SOCl₂ preferred (SO₂, HCl gases escape)
Ammonium salt; strong heat → amide (acetamide, benzamide)

cards.term: Phthalic acid + NH₃ on strong heating?
cards.definition: Ammonium phthalate → phthalamide → phthalimide
LiAlH₄ or better B₂H₆ → 1° alcohol; NaBH₄ does not reduce –COOH
It does not easily reduce esters, nitro, halo groups: selective for –COOH
Sodium salt + soda lime (NaOH : CaO = 3 : 1), heat → RH + Na₂CO₃
Electrolysis of aqueous alkali-metal carboxylates → hydrocarbon with twice the alkyl carbons
Acid with α-H + X₂ / red P, then H₂O → α-halocarboxylic acid
–COOH is deactivating, meta-directing: m-nitro- and m-bromobenzoic acid

cards.term: Why no Friedel–Crafts on benzoic acid?
cards.definition: Ring deactivated and AlCl₃ binds to the carboxyl group

Tollens’ silver mirror: Aldehydes (incl. aromatic); Fehling’s red ppt: Aliphatic aldehydes only; 2,4-DNP orange ppt: Both; Iodoform (yellow): Methyl ketones, ethanal, ethanol; NaHCO₃ effervescence: Neither (acids)
